publications.title: From reaching a shoe to keeping hold
publications.type: Frozen native comparison with independent contact audit
publications.status: 20/20 valid · 2/10 completed under both policies · 9 contact-loss alarms verified
publications.abstract: A frozen twenty-attempt native MuJoCo comparison adds continuous acquisition checks and bounded lowering to the mounted-rake PiPER controller. Both policies complete the same 2/10 fresh cases: no gains or losses. Nine bilateral-contact-loss alarms follow a trace-verified native origin by 20–52 ms, median 30 ms; three acquisition failures are separate. Twelve supported lowering responses produce no additional completion. A non-finger-support gap remains unmonitored. Complete recorded trajectories, independent audit and development failures are public. Authored policies, synthetic contact and privileged observations establish no learned skill or physical robot qualification.

publications.title: Skill prerequisites: access, reach and recovery
publications.type: Two native environments with authored policies and recorded benchmark evidence
publications.status: 16/16 valid · 2 lid contacts avoided · 3/4 retrieval checkpoints · 0/4 retained tool lifts
publications.abstract: A frozen sixteen-attempt native MuJoCo study tests hinged shoe-box access and a mounted rake for an out-of-workspace shoe. Guarded access avoids two baseline lid collisions while task completion stays at 2/4; a transient withdrawal adds 0.70 simulated seconds without being necessary in its matched baseline. The mounted rake reaches an intermediate retrieval checkpoint in 3/4 cases, but all subsequent retained lifts fail and the short-tool case is deferred. All native traces and failures remain public. The browser replays recorded states; fresh physics runs locally. Privileged observations, synthetic contact and authored policies establish no learned skill or hardware qualification.

publications.title: Live PiPER shoe workstation v0.1
publications.type: Live browser-native simulation with authored control and separate benchmark evidence
publications.status: Live browser physics · 14/16 targets · strict contact parity failed · shoe lifting unqualified
publications.abstract: A six-axis PiPER and its coupled gripper respond to user targets while MuJoCo runs locally in a browser worker. The final native run retains 20 valid attempts: 14/16 target trials pass, both high-target repeats fail, and jaw, impulse, disabled-table and 600-second hold checks pass. A ten-minute headless Chromium run reports 51.389 render calls per second and a 0.9999795 simulation/wall-time ratio on the tested Apple M5 host; simulated movement response is 61.9 ms p95 across 61 commands. Render calls do not measure GPU presentation. Native/WASM numerical and loaded-contact-count checks pass, while strict raw contact counts differ in 13/1,500 states. All fifteen development shoe-lift attempts fail. Complete development, failure and timing records remain separate. This authored rigid-shoe environment establishes no learned skill, calibrated material model or physical robot qualification.

publications.title: Reusable shoe asset library v0.1
publications.type: Versioned native scene assets and frozen passive-contact benchmark
publications.status: Six shoe proxies · three arms · support 27/27, disabled table 0/27 · manipulation unqualified
publications.abstract: Six original MIT rigid shoe proxies compose with the pinned UR5e/Robotiq, PiPER and SO-101 models through versioned scene descriptors and offline native 3D previews. A frozen 54-attempt test records 27/27 supported pairs and 0/27 support successes when table collisions are disabled; all 54 gravity checks pass without numerical warnings. No loaded non-table shoe contacts appear in the 20 ms samples, which cannot rule out shorter transients. All sampled trajectories and 27,000 native-step durations remain available. On one Apple M5 host, 54 simulated seconds take 12.3616 wall seconds including fresh model construction; the slowest attempt takes 6.7047 seconds. Geometry and physical properties are authored assumptions. Loading, gravity and passive support do not establish shoe grasping, calibrated deformation, a learned policy or hardware transfer.

publications.title: PiPER placement reliability v0.5
publications.type: Frozen paired reliability experiment with complete native evidence
publications.status: 23/36 revised grasp · 15/36 v0.4 · 8 gained, none lost · hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: Three frozen fresh PiPER cohorts retain 252 numerically valid attempts and 144 failed negative controls. A fixed diagonal grasp with bounded pose planning completes 23/36 placements versus 15/36 for frozen v0.4 and 18/36 with second-lift recovery alone: eight gained completions and none lost. The fifteen shared successes are 0.772 simulated seconds slower on average. Three lift-only second probes qualify and finish their tasks; the full grasp candidate needs none. Twelve low-friction acquisitions and one later retention failure remain. Every trajectory, native task outcome and raw computation duration is retained, including 1,035 windows exceeding 20 ms and a 3.082-second outlier on a loaded host. Native mechanics and scoring remain unchanged. Separate development keeps 200 earlier attempts, including discarded regressions. Authored privileged simulation establishes no learned skill, real-time guarantee or physical qualification.

publications.title: PiPER contact recovery v0.4
publications.type: Paired carry-recovery and supported-acquisition experiment with complete confirmation receipt
publications.status: All modes 4/12 · two resumed tasks faster · controls 0/48 · hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: A fresh frozen 84-attempt PiPER comparison completes 4/12 placements for v0.3 history, v0.4 carry-only and v0.4 full; all 48 matched open-jaw and hold controls fail. Two completed post-hold placements finish 2.440 and 2.640 simulated seconds sooner with unchanged 220/240 ms settling holds. Four low-friction failures reach refusal 2.88–2.90 seconds sooner without becoming successes. Fresh nominal-friction 60 g layouts expose two held-but-too-low resume failures in every mode; neither reaches speed restoration. Six earlier acquisition failures are traced to insufficient support under the pinned position servo and side pinch, not the actuator force cap. All native mechanics and outcome criteria remain unchanged. Complete trajectories and 84,000 raw computation windows are retained; none exceeds 20 ms on this host. Source-snapshotted development remains separate. Privileged authored simulation establishes no learned skill, true-slip accuracy or physical qualification.

publications.title: PiPER contact history v0.3
publications.type: Paired probe-only and contact-history experiment with complete confirmation receipt
publications.status: History 6/12 · baseline and probe-only 4/12 · controls 0/48 · hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: A frozen paired PiPER experiment retains all 84 numerically valid attempts across twelve synthetic rigid-block scenes. History completes 6/12 placements versus 4/12 for both original motion and the identical acquisition probe without carry monitoring; all 48 separately matched open-jaw and hold controls fail. The two added completions occur at nominal friction with 60 g blocks. Four tasks complete after five closed holds/resumes, but only four of five resume windows meet the independent low absolute TCP-speed criterion. All six supported acquisition retries fail. Native gains, forces and outcome rules remain unchanged; requested movement reduction is distinct from actual speed, and two slowdown windows include early holds. Seventy-five of 84,000 computation windows exceed 20 ms. Complete sealed trajectories, original model notices, source-snapshotted development and pinned offline inspection preserve both success and failure. Privileged authored simulation establishes no learned skill, true-slip detector accuracy, shoe competence or physical qualification.

publications.title: PiPER grip validation and recovery
publications.type: Paired authored controller experiment and complete confirmation receipt
publications.status: Moderate-friction regression · baseline 4/6, guarded 2/6 · hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: A slow test lift and bounded supported retry add recorded acquisition decisions to the pinned PiPER contact pilot, but completion regresses: at moderate friction baseline completes 2/2 and guarded completes 0/2. Both complete 2/2 normal cases; neither completes the two low-friction cases. All 30 attempts remain numerically valid, including 18 failed controls and full-duration aborts. Four qualification decisions are followed by a brief independent following window, yet two tasks still fail; no successful recovery or overall improvement is demonstrated. Actual motion continues after hold requests, and 53/30,000 computation windows exceed 20 ms. Complete compressed receipts, original model notices and pinned offline inspection preserve the evidence. Authored privileged-state simulation establishes no detector accuracy, learned shoe skill, calibrated contact or physical robot qualification.

publications.title: Native grasp task benchmark
publications.type: Native contact task implementation and authored baseline
publications.status: 6/6 simulated placements · controls 0/12 · real-time and hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: A pinned six-axis arm and coupled gripper complete 6/6 frozen synthetic rigid-block placements, while matched recorded-arm/open-jaw and hold controls complete 0/12. Native contact must produce grasp, sustained lift, retained carry, release and settled placement with tool retreat. All 18 attempts and timing traces remain in the receipt; one placement takes 29.51 wall seconds for 20 simulated seconds and misses 251 of 1,000 computation windows, so real-time operation is not established. An offline 3D mesh replay exposes the recorded motion. The authored privileged-state baseline provides a benchmark for a future compact DVIDIA action policy, not a learned footage-to-action model, validated shoe simulation or physical robot qualification.

publications.title: Hardware matched robot simulation
publications.type: Pinned mechanics implementation and CPU numerical benchmark
publications.status: Pinned CPU mechanics · PiPER contact pilot · physical fidelity unmeasured
publications.abstract: A separate UR5e/Robotiq reference preserves pinned geometry, inertias, moving-link collision proxies and coupled gripper structure: fourteen modeled coordinates and seven commands. Eighteen deterministic unloaded motion/closure runs are numerically valid; at a 1 ms step, CPU physics throughput measures 40.80–47.29 simulated seconds per measured stepping wall second on one host, excluding loading, sensing, rendering, policy and real actuation. Adjacent timestep comparisons and a matched static overlap expose numerical sensitivity and collision participation. A pure-Python paired trace scorer measures joint, tool and jaw mismatch without automatic qualification. Left/right five-finger references are separately audited; LeRobot collection with an original DVIDIA policy is proposed. Serial calibration, physical response, shoe task learning and bimanual execution remain unmeasured. An offline 3D mesh replay now exposes the recorded arm/gripper poses without rerunning physics. PiPER and SO-101 now have pinned CPU profiles with 6/6 valid unloaded numerical attempts each and explicit native command units. PiPER also has a frozen authored rigid-block contact pilot: nominal placement 2/2, low-friction placement 0/1, open-jaw 0/3 and hold 0/3, with all nine attempts numerically valid. One of 9,000 computation windows exceeds 20 ms; hardware real-time response is unqualified. SO-101 object tasks, learned policies and physical qualification remain open. YAM, OpenArm, ARX X5 and PAROL6 remain upcoming.

publications.title: DVIDIA Observation Lab pilot
publications.type: Local observation workflow and engineering feasibility pilot
publications.status: Local review release · motion and actuator source pilots · hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: DVIDIA Observation Lab supplies local object/palm proposals, reviewed timeline revisions and separate causal image-motion forecasts; real annotation and motion accuracy remain unmeasured. A new CPU pilot learns next-20-ms joint/jaw deltas from current native state and issued commands. Twelve seeded groups retain 36 recordings with 8/2/2 train/development/test grouping; 4,553 test transitions are not independent robot trials. The 6,438-byte action model computes at 0.207 ms p95 on one host and improves RMSE, while jaw MAE/worst error regress against persistence and an initial opening is substantially overpredicted. These are privileged simulator measurements and model-only timings. A proposed shoe capture plan has no footage or executed shoe benchmark. The v0.1 release and hosted synthetic review demo remain separate; no shoe policy, physical adapter, validated shoe physics or hardware qualification is established.

publications.title: Robotics research pipeline
publications.type: Architecture proposal and staged validation roadmap
publications.status: Architecture proposal · current simulation alpha · hardware unqualified
publications.abstract: An updated architecture connects immutable Skillspace recordings, reviewed task-label proposals and synchronized measured telemetry to grouped datasets, separate visual and motor learners, and a proposed local state supervisor. The implemented CPU baseline retains authored phases, gripper decisions and recovery around its learned joint-delta head. New annotation and supervisor pilots, fresh frozen confirmation, physics calibration and compatible skill-installation gates define the next milestones. Automatic labeling, learned supervision, human-video action recovery and physical arm qualification remain unestablished; this publication adds no new training or hardware result.

publications.title: Skillspace footage training pipeline
publications.type: Product implementation and measured synthetic pilot
publications.status: Public CPU package · one native scene qualified · simulation-only
publications.abstract: The public Dvidia-Inference/dvidia-training repository provides a standalone CPU pipeline that audits Skillspace media, freezes grouped splits and exports inspectable artifacts. Ten synthetic six-second clips train a visual predictor with a 0.5106-second median pipeline time across three repeats on one macOS host. Aligned native simulator telemetry supplies 4,029 training labels for a learned joint-delta head, evaluated on one held-out recording. Its capsule passes native placement qualification in that recording's exact scene; identical joint targets with open jaws fail. Installation and hardware guides accompany the package. Human-video action recovery, shoe organization, demonstration sufficiency, independent scene generalization and physical robot competence remain unestablished.

publications.title: Skill capsule acquisition and optimization
publications.type: Learned movement artifact and installation prototype
publications.status: Simulation-only · teacher/student 7/8 · no overall speedup
publications.abstract: A compact learned CPU movement head replaces joint-target computation inside an authored placement supervisor. Teacher and student both pass 7/8 in a new frozen evaluation, while episode wall time increases from 6.273 to 6.360 seconds. A 39,845-byte JSON capsule imports into the local lab, checks its exact runtime and qualifies the current scene through native placement and a recorded-arm/open-jaw control. Scene changes require a fresh test. One known scene and repeat pass native network denial; perception, complete task learning, other embodiments and hardware remain unqualified.

publications.title: Skillspace arm benchmarks and evolution
publications.type: Paired simulation benchmark and product assessment
publications.status: Mixed held-out result · 30/32 baseline, 29/32 updated
publications.abstract: Two controller revisions improve development completion from 14/20 to 17/20, but the frozen paired test declines from 30/32 to 29/32: both pass all 24 normal-strength cases while actuator-stress completion falls from 6/8 to 5/8. Instrumented CPU throughput also declines. We publish the regression, unchanged contact and success rules, exact controller snapshots, richer physical inputs, runtime-bound installation and a proposed staged Skillspace contract. Contact forces and penetration remain uncalibrated; learned perception and physical qualification are open.

publications.title: Installing a Skillspace on a simulated arm
publications.source: reports/Installing a Skillspace on a simulated arm.md
publications.type: Product prototype and native contact qualification
publications.status: Public skill link to authored adapter · 6/6 scene placements
publications.abstract: The first link-to-arm product path installs an existing DVIDIA placement envelope, binds a local authored controller to one simulated arm, and reuses it in independently grounded scenes. Native jaw contacts carry a free box; six layouts complete, while no-motion and identical joint commands with open jaws each complete zero of six. Installed execution passes process-level offline checks. Task metadata contains no learned policy; perception, cup geometry, full arm collisions and physical qualification remain open.

publications.title: Offline cable training environment
publications.type: Product prototype and local qualification
publications.status: CPU simulation-only · Controller search and frozen evaluation executed
publications.abstract: The first runnable product loop combines an anchored cable environment, local controller-parameter search, frozen evaluation, offline replay and a manifest-backed skill pack. The selected controller and a fixed feedback baseline both completed 10/10 held-out simulated episodes; zero-force and release controls completed 0/10. A native macOS network-denial run completed 3/3 additional episodes. Ideal endpoint attachment and privileged state bound the result; physical rope calibration, gripping, sensors and GPU throughput remain untested.

publications.title: Fast accurate robot training simulation
publications.type: Decision report and local experiment
publications.status: 54 CPU fixture trials · GPU and physical transfer untested
publications.abstract: A design for an offline, self-hosted training environment that turns demonstrations into calibrated practice and qualified robot skills. We examine contact, deformation, sensor feedback and the performance–accuracy tradeoff, then report 54 deterministic native MuJoCo CPU fixture trials. Fine endpoint agreement did not establish accurate contact transients, and coarse timesteps missed collisions. Minimum GPU memory, rope accuracy and physical transfer remain unmeasured.

publications.title: Grok robotics research on X
publications.type: Source review and thesis comparison
publications.status: Primary sources checked · Experiments proposed
publications.abstract: Three Grok 4.7 research passes surface observation-to-action, synthetic-practice and reusable-repair ideas. Independent primary-source checks compare those findings with our thesis: observation supplies goals and state, language retrieves a skill, spatial expectations guide attention, and executable feedback with evaluation establishes competence. X posts remain discovery leads. No universal demonstration count or arbitrary-robot transfer follows from the reviewed results.

publications.title: Spatially grounded downloadable robot skills
publications.type: Research synthesis and proposed experiments
publications.status: Source review · DVIDIA experiments not run
publications.abstract: A synthesis of learning from human demonstrations, language-conditioned spatial attention, simulation expansion and robot-specific skill delivery. Spatial priors can accelerate inspection but do not determine contact state or control. The proposed downloadable skill packages a controller, initiation and termination conditions, compatible sensing and hardware, recovery behavior and measured evidence. Separate experiments would test attention, data coverage, feedback and transfer.

publications.title: Clef and grounded video observations
publications.type: Engineering feasibility pilot
publications.status: Five licensed excerpts · Accuracy evaluation outstanding
publications.abstract: A preregistered image-API feasibility run processed five licensed three-second POV excerpts using four timestamped frames, a Gemma caption and a Clef-flash check. All five completed at a price-derived inference estimate of $0.00140634. Post-run inspection found an object error accepted by the checker and omitted state changes. API and schema compatibility were demonstrated; annotation accuracy and whole-task success were not.

publications.title: From Skillspace to robot skill
publications.type: Source review and implementation proposal
publications.status: Graduation and robot training not run
publications.abstract: An Argus review and a proposal to connect original recordings, reviewed episodes, immutable datasets, training runs, held-out evaluation and robot-tested releases. The review separates video annotation from action supervision and defines compatibility beyond a robot’s degree-of-freedom count. A proposed 40-episode annotation pilot and evidence-based graduation criteria remain unrun.

publications.title: Turn physical footage into testable evidence
publications.type: Research agenda
publications.status: Four baseline protocols proposed
publications.abstract: A research agenda covering visible capture evidence, relations over time, evaluation provenance and physical grounding. Each question has a bounded protocol and a failure condition. The aim is to measure whether structure and physical signals improve a defined task before scaling collection. Strategic opinions, author-reported results and our untested proposals are kept distinct.
